claim: Hoisting the full-window count into loop-scoped `fullWindowCount`/`samplesReadCount` assigned only inside the `ts == ev.startTimestamp || selVS.Timestamp == nil` guard makes `@`-anchored range selectors contribute nothing to the existing totalQueryableSamples after step 0, because the retained floats/histograms slices are no longer read at increment time. Measured base-vs-HEAD: predict_linear(m1[60s] @ 30, 60) drops 16 -> 4, so prometheus_engine_query_samples_total under-reports by ~numSteps and no test covers the path.
raw: #1 🔴 Critical: `@`-anchored range selectors stop counting toward the existing `totalQueryableSamples` and `prometheus_engine_query_samples_total`

claim: evalSubquery merges the subquery child's SamplesRead into the parent and then the outer range-vector loop counts the materialized matrix again via IncrementSamplesReadAtStep, so sum_over_time(m1[1m:10s]) reports samplesRead=12 against totalQueryableSamples=6, compounding to 3.8x at nesting depth 2 and 6.4x at depth 3. This exceeds TotalSamples, which the change's own struct doc says is impossible, and inflates the global prometheus_engine_query_samples_read_total counter.
raw: #2 🟠 High: `SamplesRead` double-counts subqueries, compounds with nesting depth, and exceeds `TotalSamples` — which its own struct doc says is impossible

claim: countSamplesAfter linearly rescans the entire range-vector window once per series per step (call site promql/engine.go:2164), making per-step accounting O(window x steps); nothing gates it on the promql-per-step-stats flag because the always-on SamplesRead aggregate needs it. Measured BenchmarkRangeQuery rate(a_hundred[1d]),steps=1000 goes 549-562 ms/op -> 888-894 ms/op (+58-62%) with allocations unchanged.
raw: #3 🟠 High: unconditional per-step window rescan costs 50–62% of range-query evaluation time, on a path the feature flag does not gate

claim: The added test expectations transcribe what the implementation emits rather than deriving from documented semantics, so the subquery cases encode the double count as the oracle (`SamplesRead: 2, // subquery + outer`; sum(max_over_time(...[20s:10s])) asserting TotalSamples 6 / SamplesRead 12). They will fail when the double-count bug is fixed, and no case asserts nesting depth >= 2 where the error compounds.
raw: #4 🟡 Medium: the new test expectations encode the double count as the oracle, so they will block the fix rather than catch the bug

claim: The documented contract for samplesRead is false in all four places it is stated (docs/feature_flags.md:48, docs/querying/api.md:247, util/stats/query_stats.go:279, web/api/v1/openapi_schemas.go:593): the claim that it equals totalQueryableSamples for other query types is contradicted by measurement (6 vs 12; 16 vs 4), and its placement under the promql-per-step-stats section implies a flag gate that does not exist since SamplesRead has no omitempty and is emitted for any stats value.
raw: #5 🟡 Medium: the documented contract for `samplesRead` is false, in all four places it is stated

claim: NewChildWithStepTracking for a subquery sizes two []int64 by the subquery's own step count, derived from a user-supplied resolution that no limit bounds (the API's 11000-step guard covers only the outer query). Measured instant query count_over_time(m1[10000s:1ms]) allocates +153 MB (154 MB -> 307 MB) with the flag enabled, none of it charged against query.max-samples, and half of it is the never-merged TotalSamplesPerStep array.
raw: #6 🟡 Medium: subquery per-step arrays are sized by the subquery's step count, which no limit bounds — 153 MB measured for one instant query

claim: The subquery-to-outer step mapping uses a one-to-one ceiling-division point mapping instead of distributing reads across the outer steps whose windows consume the data, so when the subquery grid is coarser than the outer grid intervening outer steps report zero reads (measured samplesReadPerStep {600:35, 630:0, 660:7}). The boundary rules also pin everything at or before startTimestamp onto step 0 and clamp everything past the last step onto it, inflating step 0 7x in the common offset case, with no caveat in the docs.
raw: #7 🟡 Medium: `samplesReadPerStep` misattributes across mismatched grids — outer steps between subquery grid points report zero reads

claim: NewChildWithStepTracking is a bare package function taking the parent's StepTrackingEnabled as a bool while its sibling NewChild is a method on *QuerySamples, so callers must hand-copy the setting and the three engine child-creation sites disagree (engine.go:1869 and :2397 use the free function, engine.go:2458 still uses ev.samplesStats.NewChild()). An external caller who forgets to thread StepTrackingEnabled() silently gets per-step tracking off.
raw: #8 🟢 Low: `NewChildWithStepTracking` is a package function while its sibling `NewChild` is a method, leaving the three child-creation sites inconsistent

claim: IncrementSamplesReadAtStep guards only the upper bound (`i < len(...)`), so a negative index still panics while an over-range index is silently dropped — giving the four increment helpers three different undocumented out-of-range contracts. The same programming error panics loudly for TotalSamples and vanishes silently for SamplesRead, breaking sum(SamplesReadPerStep) == SamplesRead with no signal.
